**"The Prophecy Problem"**

Lilac was mid-sandwich when Carol burst through the door of their treehouse base, waving a glowing crystal like a championship trophy.

"Guys. *Guys.* You will not *believe* what I found in that old Magister archive."

Milla looked up from her book, Torque from his workbench. Even Spade paused his meditation.

"A prophecy scroll," Carol announced dramatically, "about our power levels. Future us, apparently."

"That's incredibly unreliable," Spade said flatly.

"Hear me out." Carol unfurled it. "Lilac: 47 decillion. Me: 89 decillion. Torque: 23 decillion. Spade: 156 decillion—okay, *that's* hot—and then..." 

Carol's voice cracked.

"Milla: 999 decillion."

The silence was profound.

Lilac dropped her sandwich. "Say that again."

"*Nine. Hundred. Ninety-nine. Decillion.*"

Milla set down her book carefully. "That's... that seems like a lot."

"It's *six times my power level*," Spade said, standing abruptly. "Milla, you—you're the nice one. You heal things. You make tea."

"I can make very good tea," Milla offered helpfully.

"THIS ISN'T ABOUT TEA!" Carol was pacing now. "The sweet flower girl is supposedly gonna become an *interdimensional weapon*!"

Torque squinted at the scroll. "Is the decryption algorithm even reliable? Could be a typo. Maybe it said 9.99 decillion?"

"Magical prophecy scroll, Torque. Not a spreadsheet."

Lilac looked at Milla—really looked at her, as if trying to spot the dormant supernova inside her friend. "Do you... feel different?"

Milla considered this seriously. "I had extra butterflies in my cereal this morning. Does that count?"

"That's just the brand," Carol muttered.

"Here's what bothers me," Spade said, tapping the scroll. "If this is accurate, it's not random. Prophecies don't exist without causality. Something happens. Something *big*. We need to find out what—"

"Maybe I just get really good at gardening," Milla interjected brightly. "And my emotions are very powerful and flowers grow really fast and—"

"—and it cascades into reality-altering ability," Lilac finished quietly.

The treehouse felt smaller.

Carol threw up her hands. "Okay, new plan. We don't tell anyone. We lock this scroll away. We live our lives normally. When Milla eventually reaches 999 decillion, *then* we panic."

"That's the opposite of a plan," Torque said.

"It's a *feelings* plan, okay?"

But here's the thing about Milla: she'd always been underestimated. The sweet one. The healer. The gentle soul who talked to flowers and rescued creatures and radiated warmth like she was personally powered by friendship itself.

She'd never corrected anyone.

She walked to the window, looking out at the forest—the same one she'd explored since they were kids. The trees seemed a little greener when she paid attention to them. The earth felt a little warmer beneath her feet.
